html:
The First Anglo-Sikh War was fought from December 1845 to March 1846 between the Sikh Empire and the British East India Company.

After the death of Ranjit Singh in 1839, the Sikh state fell into court intrigue and the army became the main power. Fearing the army and with British forces massed on the border, the Sikh army crossed the Sutlej river in December 1845. The sides fought hard battles at Mudki, Ferozeshah, Aliwal and finally Sobraon in February 1846, which the British won.

By the Treaty of Lahore the Sikhs gave up lands, paid an indemnity and accepted a British resident at Lahore. The young ruler Duleep Singh stayed on the throne. A second war in 1848 and 1849 ended with the Punjab annexed and the Koh-i-Noor given to Queen Victoria.
sum: The First Anglo-Sikh War was fought from December 1845 to March 1846 between the Sikh Empire and the British East India Company.
